title: Reproducible Reports
summary: Why a results chapter should be built by code, and the three parts of a Quarto document: YAML, chunks and inline R.
hints: A reproducible report can be rebuilt from the raw data by running one thing, with no copying and pasting in between.
The YAML header sits between two `---` lines at the very top; chunks start with ```` ```{r} ````; inline code is `` `r ...` `` inside a sentence.
`#| include: false` runs a chunk but shows nothing; `#| echo: false` shows the results but not the code.

quiz.prompt: You fix a data-entry error in your raw file the week before your defence. Which workflow updates every number in the results chapter correctly?
choices: Rerun each SPSS analysis and retype the numbers into Word
Render the Quarto document again: the code reads the corrected file and recomputes every number
Search the Word file for the old numbers and replace them
Keep the old numbers: one row won't change anything
quiz.explain: When the numbers come from code that reads the raw data, fixing the data and rendering again updates every table, figure and sentence. Retyping is where errors creep in.

quiz.prompt: Which part of a Quarto document sets the title, author and output format?
quiz.code:
---
title: "Chapter 4: Results"
author: "A. Cadet"
format: html
---
quiz.explain: The YAML header, between two lines of `---` at the very top, holds the document's settings. Change `format: html` to `format: docx` for a Word file.

quiz.prompt: This chunk loads packages and reads the data. What appears in the finished report?
quiz.code:
```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(readr)
crew <- read_csv("astronauts.csv")
```
choices: Nothing, but `crew` exists for the chunks after it
Nothing, and the code doesn't run
quiz.explain: `include: false` runs the chunk and keeps its objects, but shows neither code nor output. `eval: false` is the one that skips running.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence will always match the data?
choices: The log holds `r format(nrow(crew), big.mark = ",")` missions.
quiz.explain: Inline code is a backtick, the letter r, a space, the code and a closing backtick. Without the `r` it is just code formatting, and a typed number goes stale when the data change.

quiz.prompt: Your committee asks for the tables but not the R code. Which chunk option fits?
quiz.explain: `echo: false` hides the code and keeps the output. `include: false` would hide the table too; `eval: false` wouldn't run the code at all.
